paper.title_en: Four-Point String Monodromy from Six-Point Supersymmetric Consistency
paper.abstract_en: Can finite-particle consistency determine an infinite string amplitude? For four-dimensional planar tree-level $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills effective theories with a specified scalar parity condition, we derive all-order constraints directly from physical six-point Ward identities and local factorization. An overlapping-channel limit forces a scalar cocycle, while an explicit differential Ward functional eliminates all relevant five- and six-point contact freedom and fixes the four-point kernel by $q''=-6c_{00}q$. Its normalized branches are linear, trigonometric, and hyperbolic, and the target amplitude obeys the associated four-point monodromy. If its entire pole-subtracted axis sequence additionally admits one common nonzero positive moment measure, the trigonometric branch is selected and the complete Veneziano low-energy germ is unique up to scale. The result separates a formal low-energy necessity theorem from its conditional analytic-germ uniqueness corollary; no worldsheet or auxiliary KLT-module membership is assumed for the physical theorem.
